text:
sec-bot: [gitleaks] detected possible npm publish token in monorepo/packages/auth/package.json (commit 6a1f2c). token pattern matches npm:_authToken. suspicious publish event: package@1.2.3 published 2 days ago. link: https://internal-alerts.example.com/alert/4832

maria: seeing it. tagging owners. @jesse are you able to confirm ownership of that package?

jesse: yep that's my package. i pushed a feature branch last month, didn't expect creds in package.json. looking now.

oliver: quick note — CI stores npm auth in GH Actions secrets for the legacy workflow. can someone check whether the token in package.json matches an active secret?

raj: on it. checking GH secrets and actions logs. also verifying runner cache/artifacts for leaked tokens.

maria: action plan: 1) revoke token 2) verify npm registry activity and package integrity 3) rotate CI secrets and purge caches 4) audit similar packages for hardcoded tokens 5) file incident ticket. assigning: @jesse revoke token + confirm local/dev machines, @raj sweep CI and purge caches, @oliver update workflows to use repo-level secret and least-priv tokens, @devx add a scan rule to catch npm:_authToken in JSON files.

jesse: i've revoked the token at npmjs (revoked id: npm-token-042). npm shows one publish event from the token: 2024-08-10T14:02:17Z for version 1.2.3. i'm starting a package integrity check (tarball hash) and will compare published artifact to our build outputs.

raj: GH secrets: no active repo secret matches the leaked token. however older workflow logs contain the token in runner stdout in run-2023-11-09-abcdef.tar.gz in actions artifacts. i've queued a purge of artifacts for affected runs and requested audit logs from GH for token usage.

devx: i pushed a quick gitleaks rule update to the nightly scan to flag `"_authToken"` patterns in JSON files and add package.json to high-priority checks. PR: https://git.redwood/sig/devexp/gitleaks-rules/pull/12

jessica: legal/compliance note — any public download of the package that could have included modified code must be assessed. when you have the integrity check results share with me and i'll advise on disclosure requirements.

maria: integrity results?

jesse: tarball hash check done. published tarball matches our build output for 1.2.3 — no tamper. looks like token was only used for a normal publish. no malicious versions detected.

oliver: good. still need to rotate CI secrets and make sure runners don't cache secrets in logs. @raj can you push stricter masking for action logs and forbid printing envs?

raj: yes — added `ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG=false` enforcement via org policy and updated runner masking rules. also added a job to scrub artifacts older than 30 days. deployed change to infra this morning.

maria: documentation of containment steps so we can close the incident: revoked npm token, purged GH artifacts, rotated CI secrets, enforced runner masking, added gitleaks rule, audited other packages in monorepo (no other tokens found), validated published artifact integrity, notified legal. anything missing?

devx: i'll create a post-incident checklist item to add npm package owner onboarding with guidance: never commit tokens, prefer short-lived tokens with publish scope, use org-scoped npm access tokens.

jessica: thanks — i'll prepare a quick compliance note summarizing timeline and actions for SOC records.

maria: thanks all. closing on our side pending jesse confirmation that local devs rotated any cached tokens.

jesse: confirmed — i asked the team to rotate their local npm tokens and cleared stored tokens in dev machines. all set from my side. :white_check_mark:

sec-bot: incident ticket ENGSEC-2024-319 updated: status = contained, severity = low, actions recorded in ticket.

maria: closing thread. follow-up action items: devexp PR merged, infra masking deployed, security rule added. i'll add a short blameless retro in next security sync. :memo:
